name: Virginia
basePeriod: The first four of the last five completed calendar quarters before your claim. Virginia uses the four most recent completed quarters only if those do not qualify.
notModeled: Claims filed before July 5, 2026 use the earlier table, $112 to $430 a week.
The alternate base period: enter whichever four quarters the VEC will use.

citation.sourceDocument: Code of Virginia §§60.2-602, 60.2-607, 60.2-612; the §60.2-602 Benefit Table (July 2026), VEC
citation.sourceNote: VEC: "For new claims filed on or after July 5, 2026: The maximum weekly benefit amount increases to $478, while the minimum increases to $160", and "you must have earned at least $3,000 in your two highest paying quarters combined." §60.2-602 makes the weekly amount the table's, and §60.2-607 its duration, "not exceed[ing] twenty-six times" it. All 319 rows and 4,785 duration cells of the table were checked on 2026-10-19 against a closed form: $160 for $3,000 to $3,050 of two-quarter wages, $1 more for each $50 started above $3,050, to $478; and with the row's base B ($3,000 plus $50 a row), n weeks from 12 to 26 need base-period wages over B + B × (n - 12) / 14, rounded to the dollar. §60.2-612: wages in at least two quarters; one unpaid waiting week.
